summary:
US tariffs and Section 301 duties add paperwork and planning complexity, including product life cycle disclosure.
Bangladesh's February 2026 deal sets the tariff at 19 per cent, after 20 per cent from August 2025 and a proposed 37 per cent.
Zero-duty access covers only apparel using US cotton or man-made fibre within a volume still being finalised; EU-bound programmes keep Chinese inputs.

summary:

 Across 5,000 sqm, visitors will experience new machinery, textile applications and production solutions.
It will prioritise the anniversary programme over ITMA 2027 in Hanover, while presenting new developments at ITMA ASIA 2026 in Shanghai and Changzhou.

title: ICE cotton gains on US export sales; harvest pressure persists
summary:
ICE December 2026 cotton settled 42 points higher at 83.31 cents per pound, its third gain this week after recent sharp losses.
US Upland cotton net sales rose to 230,517 bales in the week ended September 17, supporting futures as harvest supplies advance.
China reserve auctions showed strong uptake, but softer domestic spot indices and lower crude oil may limit cotton’s recovery.

title: Bangladesh sets up five panels to strengthen trade logistics
summary:
Bangladesh has set up five working groups to put the National Logistics Policy 2025 into action for trade and supply-chain efficiency.
The panels cover digitalisation, investment, skills, multimodal infrastructure and trade facilitation, areas critical to apparel exports.
The move follows warnings that high logistics costs and port delays are hurting competitiveness.

title: Europe 2026 growth forecast lifted on resilient demand: S&P Global
summary:
S&P Global Ratings now expects eurozone and UK GDP to grow 0.9 per cent and 1.3 per cent in 2026, respectively, after stronger demand.
The upgrade signals firmer near-term European consumer markets, but savings-led spending may fade as fiscal support expires.
For sourcing and retail planners, stickier inflation, higher rates, gas assumptions and currency shifts keep risks elevated.

title: India’s FY27 growth forecast raised to 7.1% by OECD
summary:
India’s economy is projected to grow by 7.1 per cent in FY2026-27, retaining the strongest G20 outlook after an OECD forecast upgrade. 
US growth is forecast at 2.2 per cent in 2026, China’s at 4.5 per cent and global growth at 2.9 per cent.
Higher energy costs, trade uncertainty and inflation remained risks, while resilient domestic demand  supported India’s economic momentum.

title: Netherlands' GDP growth revised to 0.6% in Q2 2026
summary:
Second official estimate puts Netherlands GDP growth at 0.6 per cent in Q2 2026 versus Q1, above the 0.4 per cent first estimate.
The revision reflects stronger exports, particularly services, and higher household consumption, useful for European demand planning.
Jobs rose by 15,000 quarter on quarter, reversing an initial estimate of an 8,000 decline.

title: Can Indonesia keep importing $4.56 bn of fabric for $8.7 bn apparel?
summary:
Indonesia imported $4.56 billion of fabric in 2025 and exported $801 million, leaving a $3.76 billion deficit.
Apparel exports reached $8.70 billion against $665 million of imports, generating an $8.04 billion surplus, with the US buying 56.4 per cent.
Jakarta is considering state-backed textile capacity, but mills must compete on price, quality, specifications and delivery.

title: Bangladesh Bank keeps rate unchanged at 9.5% amid inflation pressure
summary:
Bangladesh Bank has kept its policy interest rate unchanged at 9.5 per cent as it assesses domestic and global shocks affecting inflation and growth. 
The MPC noted easing headline inflation but flagged risks from Middle East conflicts, higher fuel prices and the new national pay scale. 
For textile and apparel supply chains, borrowing costs remain unchanged while energy volatility stays a key risk.

title: Apparel M&A opens a new sourcing power equation for suppliers
summary:
Deals from August 10 to September 1 link Marc Jacobs, Untuckit, Roots and Edward Segal in apparel and textile M&A.
Marc Jacobs and Roots separate brand stewardship from operating execution, while Randa keeps Untuckit stand-alone.
Capstone Partners says five leading brand aggregators have announced or completed 29 apparel, footwear and accessories acquisitions since 2023.

title: Japan’s apparel imports grow 6.6% to $2.3 bn in July 2026
summary:
Japan's apparel and accessories imports rose 6.6 per cent year on year to 371,963 million yen (~$2.36 billion) in August 2026.
Textile yarn and fabric imports climbed 16.9 per cent, while exports grew 10.4 per cent during the month.
Textile machinery exports rose 24.0 per cent to 27,984 million yen in August and 11.7 per cent to 160,129 million yen in January-June 2026.

title: EU Philippines FTA opens €514 mn apparel sourcing opportunity
summary:
EU-Philippines FTA talks reached substantial agreement on September 22, 2026, with over 94 per cent of tariff lines expected to be liberalised.
TexPro shows H1 2026 EU27 imports from the Philippines up 45.8 per cent in HS6110 sweaters, 16.7 per cent in HS6203 and 10.0 per cent in HS6204.
Rules of origin, capacity and compliance will decide if preferential access becomes durable EU business.

title: Luxury demand polarises: How is the fashion supply chain responding?
summary:
First-half 2026 results show luxury demand concentrating at the top end as higher prices and softer discretionary spending curb aspirational buyers.
Prada Group revenue rose 16 per cent at constant exchange rates to €3.048 billion (~$3.46 billion), while Hermès grew 6.1 per cent.
Moncler EMEA, Ferragamo wholesale and Gucci show pressure, prompting reassessment of pricing, product mix and distribution.

title: New Look, M&S, Sainsbury’s, Oxfam launch UK textile recycling plan
summary:
New Look, M&S, Sainsbury’s, Oxfam and Circle-8 have announced The Circuit to build UK circular textile value chains.
It will recover, sort and pre-process non-reusable end-of-use textiles into feedstock for fibre to fibre recycling.
The first phase starts in January 2027 at Oxfam’s Batley site, testing automated sorting, traceability and scale-up models.

title: Climate Pledge Fashion Coalition targets net zero fashion by 2040
summary:
The Climate Pledge, Amazon, Stella McCartney and Canopy have launched a Fashion Coalition, with World Economic Forum support, to help more than 60 signatories reach net-zero carbon by 2040.
The group will aggregate demand, develop blended finance and offer tools intended to commercialise lower-carbon materials, technologies and supply chains.

title: Global supply shifts open growth window for Indian apparel: Report
summary:
India held about 3 per cent of global apparel exports in 2025, while China’s share fell to 27.3 per cent from 36.9 per cent in 2010, PL Capital said.
Bangladesh and Vietnam have captured more of the shift, lifting their combined share to over 13 per cent.
Trade access, China+1 sourcing and policy support could favour large, integrated Indian garment exporters.

title: China gains as Bangladesh loses share in Denmark apparel market
summary:
Denmark’s apparel imports fell 4.9 per cent to $2.595 billion in January–June 2026 from $2.728 billion a year earlier.
China’s shipments rose 5.4 per cent to $568.519 million, lifting its share to 21.91 per cent; Bangladesh fell 13.1 per cent to $438.509 million.
Germany stayed third, Sweden moved close behind and Poland ranked fifth as the top five suppliers held 62.81 per cent of imports.

title: New Zealand’s apparel imports rise 5.8% in August 2026
summary:
New Zealand’s apparel imports rose 5.8 per cent to NZ$180.01 million in August 2026.
January–August imports slipped 0.7 per cent to NZ$1.377 billion as the decline narrowed from 1.6 per cent.
Knitted or crocheted fabric imports fell 12.4 per cent in August but rose 12.5 per cent in January–August.
Apparel exports fell 5.8 per cent in August, though January–August exports edged up 0.1 per cent.

title: Pearl Global commissions new garment manufacturing unit in Bangladesh
summary:
Pearl Global Industries has commissioned a new garment facility and expanded sustainable laundry capacity in Bangladesh. 
The unit adds about 7 million pieces of annual garment capacity, taking total installed capacity to about 108 million pieces per annum. 
The laundry expansion is expected to improve efficiency, reduce washing costs and water use, and generate ROCE of about 18-20 per cent.

title: Heat is erasing 4.1% of Bangladesh garment factory revenue
summary:
Cornell research across eight Dhaka-region garment factories estimates heat erased 4.1 per cent of annual revenue on average.
Most cooling investments studied could pay back within one to four years; TexPro says 81.6 per cent of H1 2026 value was in the EU27, US, UK and Canada.
Pricing pressure, a 17.4 per cent diesel rise and power risks make passive cooling and shared adaptation finance key.
